description: We're a team from Chihuahua, Mexico, building AnalogFinder: an interactive map that ranks places on Earth by how similar they are to Moon and Mars sites, and shows where the analogy breaks down. Our team is already complete! Together we bring software and coding, AI/ML, data management, statistics, graphic design, video and photography, writing and communications, and business skills. We're excited to spotlight lesser-known analogs from northern Mexico using open NASA data. 🚀
summary: This project identifies and compares regions of the Earth that resemble the surfaces of the Moon and Mars, with the aim of proposing sites at which equipment, procedures, and technologies can be tested before they are sent into space. Testing on Earth is less costly and safer, and it allows experiments to be repeated. The outcome will be a comparative catalog of analog sites, together with the criteria that justify the selection of each one.
details: The project is an interactive globe that compares regions of the Earth with the Moon and Mars, to help choose sites for testing space technology. Each analog site is scored on geology, climate, relief, isolation, accessibility, and safety, using NASA POWER climate data, and users explore and compare the sites on the globe. It lowers the cost and risk of space testing by guiding teams to the right Earth site first, and it can be expanded with new sites, including in Mexico and Latin America. It was built with Cursor and Claude, using TypeScript, Next.js, React, Tailwind CSS, MapLibre, and NASA POWER data stored in JSON files.
